props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

bestPractices.text: Put a `Container` inside; one idea per Section.
Add your own padding or margin to a Section.

rules: Fills the viewport width; vertical padding only (80 / 84 / 141 / 176 px at 360 / 768 / 1280 / 1920).

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <Section><Container><Heading>Where we build</Heading></Container></Section>

entries.name: Stack
entries.summary: Children in a column with an even gap taken from the spacing tokens.
notes: Spacing comes from the tokens, so it changes in one place.

examples.title: Basic usage
examples.code: <Stack gap={5}><Card …/><Card …/></Stack>

entries.name: Text
entries.summary: Text in one of the three voices: body, lead, small, caption, or the mono uppercase label. Tone is an opacity of white (strong, default, dim) or red. New in this library.
entries.description:
Text in one of the three voices (Inter for reading, JetBrains Mono for labels): variant 'body' (16 px, loose) · 'lead' (the sentence under a title) · 'small' (14 px) 'caption' (12 px) · 'label' (mono, uppercase, tracked) tone 'default' (65 % white) · 'strong' (100 %) · 'dim' (50 %) · 'red' measure cap the line at 62ch Renders a `

` (a `` for `label`); `as` overrides it.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

bestPractices.text: Use `measure` for any paragraph wider than a column.
Use `dim` for anything a reader needs: 50 % white is for captions.

rules: Block-level (`label` is inline).

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <Text variant="lead" measure>The sentence under a title.</Text>

entries.name: VisuallyHidden
entries.summary: Text for assistive technology that is not drawn: the “Close” on an icon-only button, the “(current page)” after a link. It stays in the reading order and out of the layout.
notes: Prefer a visible label wherever there is room for one.
The same utility is the sr-only class used across the site.

examples.title: Basic usage

entries.name: Accordion
entries.summary: A disclosure list with real height animation: index, title and a mono code per row; the code scrambles on hover or focus, the plus turns, the body opens with eased height.
entries.description:
Disclosure list with real height animation. Each row: index, title, optional
meta; the header scrambles its meta code on hover/focus, the plus turns, the
body opens with eased height + opacity (never a jump).

items: [{ id, title, meta, body }]   body: string | node
single: only one row open at a time (default true)

props.name: items
props.description: `body` is a string or any node.

props.name: single
props.description: Only one row open at a time.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The `id` of the row that starts open.

keyboard.does: Open or close the focused row.

bestPractices.text: Use it for 3–8 related rows of short text.
Hide content a reader needs to compare — use a table.

rules: Fills its parent. Put it in a column no narrower than 20rem.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <Accordion defaultOpen="one" items={[{ id: 'one', title: 'Scope', meta: 'S-01', body: 'Say what the system will do.' }]} />

entries.name: ArrowLink
entries.summary: An inline call to action: an underline draws left→right on hover and the arrow glides out of its corner. Becomes a router Link (`to`), an external link (`href`) or a button.

props.name: href
props.description: External or `mailto:` URL; `https:` links open in a new tab.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

bestPractices.text: One per block, at the end of the thought it belongs to.
Use it as a button for something that is not navigation.

rules: Intrinsic and inline: it sits in a sentence or a `Cluster`. Do not give it a width.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <ArrowLink to="/systems">Read the principles</ArrowLink>

entries.name: CompareSlider
entries.summary: Before / after comparison. Drag the handle (mouse, touch, pen), press the track to glide there, or use ← → Home End on the handle.
entries.description:
Before / after comparison. Drag the handle (mouse, touch, pen), press the
track to glide there, or use ← → Home End on the handle. The position is a
registered CSS variable, so clicking the track or using the keyboard EASES
the reveal instead of snapping; while dragging the ease is off so the handle
tracks the finger exactly.

props.name: before
props.description: The left layer. Fill it with `position: absolute; inset: 0`.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

rules: Fills its parent and keeps a fixed ratio; give it a parent 20–46rem wide. Both layers must fill the box.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: } after={} />

entries.name: DragRail
entries.summary: A horizontal rail of cards. Touch scrolls natively with snap; with a mouse you can grab and fling it. The rail is a named, keyboard-scrollable region.
entries.description:
A horizontal rail of cards. Touch scrolls natively with snap. With a mouse
you can grab and fling it: drag moves the rail 1:1 and release carries on
with momentum that decays smoothly. Also: ← → buttons, arrow keys on the
focused rail, and a progress thumb that tracks position. A drag never fires
the click on the card underneath.

props.name: children
props.description: The cards. Give each a fixed width (≈ 16–22rem).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrollable region.

keyboard.does: Scroll the rail when it has focus.

rules: The rail fills its parent; its **children** carry the width. Use cards 16–22rem wide.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <DragRail label="Case studies">{items.map((i) => <Card key={i.id} title={i.title} />)}</DragRail>

entries.name: GlideTabs
entries.summary: A segmented control / tab list whose selection ink glides between tabs. Full tablist keyboard model; pass `panels={false}` when it only changes a nearby demo (then it is announced as a radio group).
entries.description:
Segmented control / tab list whose selection ink GLIDES from tab to tab
(shared layout animation) instead of toggling. Full tablist keyboard model:
← → Home End move and select, only the selected tab is in the tab order.

`idPrefix` lets the panel it controls point back at its tab:
tab id   `${idPrefix}-tab-${id}`     panel id `${idPrefix}-panel-${id}`

When nothing is a tab panel — the control only changes what a nearby demo
shows — pass `panels={false}`: it is then announced as a radio group (one

entries.description:
A number that rolls into place, each digit on its own wheel with a stagger.
The wheels start at 0 and settle when the number scrolls into view; a CSS
transition does all of the motion. Reads as the plain number to assistive

entries.name: ProximityText
entries.summary: Text that reacts to the pointer: each unit lifts, swells and warms toward red as the cursor comes near. Touch and reduced motion get plain text.
entries.description:
Text that reacts to the pointer: each unit lifts, swells and warms toward red
as the cursor comes near, so a sweep across a headline rolls through it like
a wave and settles back smoothly when the cursor leaves.

by="word"  (default) — keeps the font's kerning intact; right for display serif
by="char"            — per letter; right for mono labels and short words

The engine is useProximity (one rAF loop, only while something is moving).
Touch devices and reduced motion get plain static text. The full string is
exposed to assistive tech via the hidden twin; the animated spans are
aria-hidden.

props.name: radius
props.description: Reach of the effect in px.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

rules: Inline-block units that wrap with the parent; set the font size on a parent (`.heading-1`).

entries.name: ScrambleText
entries.summary: Text that decodes from noise into its final form, left to right. Shows the final text at once under reduced motion.
entries.description:
Text that decodes from noise into its final form, left to right.

trigger  change this value (e.g. increment a counter on hover) to replay
auto     also play once when the text first scrolls into view

The scramble is written straight to the DOM (no React state), uses a
deterministic glyph sequence (no randomness during render), and the real
string is always present for assistive tech in a hidden twin. Reduced motion
shows the final text with no scramble.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

rules: Reserve the final width: the scramble uses the same width as the text. Mono labels work best.

entries.description:

stretches and lights, hover/focus names it, click glides there (through the
same smooth scroller as the rest of the site). Desktop only — it never

sections: [{ id, label }]   ids are DOM ids on the section elements

entries.name: ScrollWords

entries.description:
A passage that lights up word by word as you scroll through it — reading
pace becomes scroll pace. One ScrollTrigger writes a single --p (0..1) onto
the element; every word derives its own opacity from --p and its index in
CSS, so there is no per-word JS. Wrap a word in *asterisks* to give it the
accent when lit. Reduced motion shows the whole passage lit.

entries.description:
A card whose 1px border and surface are lit by the pointer: a radial light
travels the border while a faint glow pools under the cursor. The border is
the card's own background showing through a 1px inset (no CSS mask, so it is
cheap), and the light follows --mx/--my from usePointerField.

Polymorphic: `to` -> router Link, `href` -> <a>, otherwise <div>.
`tone="red"` lights the border red (default), `"white"` for a quieter card.

entries.name: TiltSurface
entries.summary: A surface that leans toward the pointer, with a specular highlight that follows it. Driven by CSS variables (no React state); touch and reduced motion get a still surface. Children may use `data-depth="n"` to drift against the tilt.
entries.description: A surface that leans toward the pointer, with a specular highlight that follows it. The tilt, the highlight and the return to rest are all driven by the --px/--py variables from usePointerField (a CSS transition on those registered properties does the easing), so there is no per-frame JS easing and no React state. Touch devices and reduced motion get a still surface. Children may use `data-depth="n"` to drift against the tilt (parallax): …

props.name: tilt
props.description: Maximum lean in degrees. 7 by default.

props.name: ...rest

entries.name: VelocityMarquee
entries.summary: A marquee that reads the page’s scroll. It drifts on its own, speeds up and leans with scroll velocity, and slows under the pointer. Reduced motion shows the first set, still.
entries.description:
A marquee that reads the page's scroll. It drifts on its own, speeds up and
leans (skew) with scroll velocity from Lenis, and eases to a crawl under the
pointer — so scrolling the page visibly pushes the ribbon along. It only
ticks while on screen. Reduced motion shows the first set, still.

entries.name: Button
entries.summary: The primary interactive control. It becomes a router `Link` with `to`, an `<a>` with `href` (external links open safely in a new tab) and a `<button>` otherwise. Magnetic pull toward the pointer by default.
entries.description:
Primary interactive control. Resolves its element automatically:
to    -> react-router <Link>
href  -> <a> (external / mailto)
else  -> <button>

Props:
variant  'primary' | 'ghost' | 'line' | 'outline'   (default 'primary')
size     'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'                          (default 'md')
icon     optional lucide icon component
magnetic enable magnetic pull                        (default true)

props.name: variant
props.description: One `primary` per view; the rest `line` or `ghost`.

props.name: magnetic
props.description: The pointer pull. Turn it off in dense UI and inside forms.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

bestPractices.text: One `primary` button per region; the second action is `line`.
Set a width. A full-width button is a `Stack` child.
Use a button for navigation: use `to`/`href`.

rules: Intrinsic. Label is mono, `--fs-2xs`, uppercase; padding grows sm → md → lg. Hit area is ≥ 44px tall.

examples.code: <Button to="/contact">Start a conversation</Button>

entries.name: EngineAnatomy
entries.summary: How the engine is organised, as an interactive blueprint. Pick a part on the left; the matching block on the diagram lights and the panel explains it. The only external link on the whole site lives here — to the YK Engine repository.
entries.description:
How the engine is organised, as an interactive blueprint. Pick a part on the
left; the matching block on the diagram lights and the panel explains it.
The only external link on the whole site lives here — to the YK Engine
repository.

parts: [{ id, name, glyph, line, detail, folders }]

entries.name: EngineAside
entries.summary: Hero object for YK Engine: a framed miniature viewport that leans toward the pointer. Decoration drawn to evoke an engine viewport — not engine output.

entries.name: EnginePipeline
entries.summary: A left-to-right flow of stages. Pick one (click, tap, or ← →) and a token glides along the line to it — the line fills behind it — while the panel below cross-slides to that stage's description.
entries.description:
A left-to-right flow of stages. Pick one (click, tap, or ← →) and a token
glides along the line to it — the line fills behind it — while the panel
below cross-slides to that stage's description. The shared-data stage is the
hinge: it is the same set of entities and components either side.

stages: [{ id, label, glyph, title, body, points }]

entries.name: ExperienceStoryboard
entries.summary: A storyboard of the shopping and transaction experience, from first look to confirmation. Five abstract frames, each with one small interaction; a scrubber and ← → move through them, and Play walks the whole journey.
entries.description:
A storyboard of the shopping and transaction experience, from first look to
confirmation. Five abstract frames, each with one small interaction; a
scrubber and ← → move through them, and Play walks the whole journey. It is
an illustration of the *experience* — shapes, not screenshots.

stages: [{ id, label, glyph, title, body }]

entries.name: FaqDesk
entries.summary: Questions and answers with a desk of categories on the left and a search field above the list. Type to narrow, pick a category, open a question; each answer can point at the page that answers it properly.
entries.description:
Questions and answers with a desk of categories on the left and a search
field above the list. Type to narrow, pick a category, open a question; each
answer can point at the page that answers it properly.

faqs: [{ id, cat, q, a: string | string[], to?, toLabel? }]

entries.name: FrameBudget
entries.summary: The frame budget, measured rather than described. Choose how many boxes to animate and which property moves them; press Run and the page really animates them for a couple of seconds while counting the frames it manages.
entries.description:
The frame budget, measured rather than described. Choose how many boxes to
animate and which property moves them; press Run and the page really animates
them for a couple of seconds while counting the frames it manages. The result
is a measurement of YOUR device, right now — and says so.

entries.name: GateWalk
entries.summary: "Each stage gates the next." Walk a system from intent to release: the runner can only pass a gate once everything that gate asks has been ticked. Passing a gate glides the runner to the next stage; the last one releases.
entries.description:
"Each stage gates the next." Walk a system from intent to release: the
runner can only pass a gate once everything that gate asks has been ticked.
Passing a gate glides the runner to the next stage; the last one releases.
A way of working shown as a game — not a certification and not a record of
any real release.

stages: [{ id, title, body, glyph, gates: [string] }]

entries.name: GlossaryBrowser
entries.summary: Every term the site uses, in plain language: search, filter by area, jump by letter, copy a link to one term. The same list explains the words that are underlined in the guides.

entries.name: HiringPath
entries.summary: What a conversation about working at North looks like, stage by stage, from either side of the table. Pick a stage on the path; flip between "you" and "us" to read what each side does. No roles are open, and no timings are given.
entries.description:
What a conversation about working at North looks like, stage by stage, from
either side of the table. Pick a stage on the path; flip between "you" and
"us" to read what each side does. No roles are open, and no timings are given.

stages: [{ id, name, line, you[], us[], stops }]

entries.name: IdempotencyDemo
entries.summary: A payment request whose answer gets lost on the way back. With no idempotency key the client retries and the customer is charged twice; with one, the server recognises the retry and replays its first answer.
entries.description:
A payment request whose answer gets lost on the way back. With no
idempotency key the client retries and the customer is charged twice; with
one, the server recognises the retry and replays its first answer. Press Pay,
flip the key on and off, and watch the ledger.

entries.name: IdentityCard
entries.summary: Hero object for the Company page: a card that leans toward the pointer and turns over on click / Enter / Space. Front: the mark and status. Back: the company and its development team, each one a link.

entries.name: InsightLibrary
entries.summary: The guides, as a library: filter by area, search, sort by length, and see at a glance which ones have something to play with. Titles, summaries and reading times are read from the guides themselves.

entries.name: IntegrationAtlas
entries.summary: Six ways to connect two systems, and two of them at a time. Choose any two and every row compares them. The entries are general reference, written for this site, not a statement about any particular integration.
entries.description:
Six ways to connect two systems, and two of them at a time. Choose any two and
every row compares them. The entries are general reference, written for this
site, not a statement about any particular integration.

patterns: [{ id, name, how, speed, coupling, fails, effort, use, avoid }]

entries.name: KeyboardMap
entries.summary: A keyboard you can press — or tap. Each key that does something on this site is drawn as a keycap; press the real key (or tap the cap) and it lights and says what it does here.
entries.description:
A keyboard you can press — or tap. Each key that does something on this site
is drawn as a keycap; press the real key (or tap the cap) and it lights and
says what it does here. Keys are only listened to while the map is on screen
and never while you are typing in a field; nothing is intercepted, so Tab and
the rest keep doing their job.

keys: [{ id, label, wide?, match: [event.key], does }]   rows: [[id, id, …], …]

entries.name: KitIndex
entries.summary: The front door of the interface kit: every component, found by name or by what it is for. With nothing typed it shows the six families (each with its count and a few of its components);
entries.description:
The front door of the interface kit: every component, found by name or by what
it is for. With nothing typed it shows the six families (each with its count and
a few of its components); as you type it becomes a list of matches that link
straight to the component, open in its family's gallery.

entries.name: LayerStack
entries.summary: An exploded view of a layered system. Three plates start stacked and part as you scroll through the section (one ScrollTrigger writes --p, CSS does the rest); hover or focus a plate to lift it clear and read what it holds.
entries.description:
An exploded view of a layered system. Three plates start stacked and part as
you scroll through the section (one ScrollTrigger writes --p, CSS does the
rest); hover or focus a plate to lift it clear and read what it holds. Built
in CSS 3D from three static elements — no canvas, no per-frame JS.

layers: [{ code, title, body, glyph }]   top plate first

entries.name: LegalCentre
entries.summary: Every legal document in one place. The title, section count and reading time of each card are read from the document itself, and the bar along the bottom is its shape: one segment per section, as wide as the section is long.
entries.description:
Every legal document in one place. The title, section count and reading time
of each card are read from the document itself, and the bar along the bottom
is its shape: one segment per section, as wide as the section is long.

docs: [{ key, kind, blurb }]   (kind: Policy · Notice · Statement)

entries.name: LicenceTable
entries.summary: Every library and typeface the site is built with, its version and its licence, as published by the packages themselves. Filter, search, sort — and see at a glance which licences make up the whole.

entries.name: LifecycleLine
entries.summary: A system's life as five stages, with an illustrative shape of the effort each asks for. Slide along it to see where you are and what the stage is mostly about.
entries.description:
A system's life as five stages, with an illustrative shape of the effort each
asks for. Slide along it to see where you are and what the stage is mostly
about. The shape is qualitative: it says which stages tend to be larger, not by
how much.

stages: [{ id, name, years, blurb, mostly, decisions, risks, effort: [number x 10] }]

entries.name: LiveBudget
entries.summary: Live numbers from THIS page on THIS device: frames per second, how many background scenes are actually running (against the cap), how many animation loops are subscribed and the current quality tier.
entries.description:
Live numbers from THIS page on THIS device: frames per second, how many
background scenes are actually running (against the cap), how many animation
loops are subscribed and the current quality tier. Read twice a second,
written straight to the DOM, and only while the panel is on screen. The
button pauses every background so you can watch the numbers move.
`framed` gives it a card of its own (used as a hero object).

entries.name: LiveStatus
entries.summary: Not a status page for the company — a status page for YOUR visit.
entries.description:
Not a status page for the company — a status page for YOUR visit. Everything
on it is measured by your own browser, live: the frame rate of this very
page, how the page loaded, what the connection looks like, and (when you ask)
how long a small request to the site's own host takes. It says nothing about
anyone else's experience, and says so.

entries.name: LogoPlate
entries.summary: Hero object for the Musebase page: the real mark, set on a light plate like a physical card, in front of two more plates (the mark itself is a stack of planes).
entries.description:
Hero object for the Musebase page: the real mark, set on a light plate like a
physical card, in front of two more plates (the mark itself is a stack of
planes). The set leans toward the pointer and each plate drifts at its own
depth against the tilt. Falls back to a wordmark if the logo asset is absent.

entries.name: MiniEngine
entries.summary: A miniature 2D scene — rectangles and discs drifting in a grid, one of them "selected" with a gizmo that hops between them. It is decoration drawn to evoke an engine viewport; it does not run YK Engine.
entries.description:
A miniature 2D scene — rectangles and discs drifting in a grid, one of them
"selected" with a gizmo that hops between them. It is decoration drawn to
evoke an engine viewport; it does not run YK Engine. It draws on the shared
frame scheduler at ~30fps and only while on screen; reduced motion renders one
still frame.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

entries.name: NeedsFinder
entries.summary: "What are you trying to do?" — pick a need and the matching system area is lit in the strip below and explained in the panel, with a link. A small playful route through the section, built as a real radio group (↑ ↓ ← → move and choose;
entries.description:
"What are you trying to do?" — pick a need and the matching system area is
lit in the strip below and explained in the panel, with a link. A small
playful route through the section, built as a real radio group (↑ ↓ ← → move
and choose; the choice announces itself).

needs: [{ id, label, area, why }]     areas: [{ id, code, title, glyph, to }]

entries.name: NorthCompass
entries.summary: Hero object for the development page: a compass whose four points are the four pillars of the team's work.
entries.description:
Hero object for the development page: a compass whose four points are the
four pillars of the team's work. The needle follows the pointer around the
dial (CSS-eased, always the short way round) and the pillar it settles on
is the one described below. Tap or focus a point to turn the needle to it.
Leaving the dial lets the needle settle back on the nearest pillar.

pillars: [{ id, code, title, body }]  (four — N, E, S, W in that order)

entries.name: OpsFlow
entries.summary: "The life of a request." Choose a kind of request and send it: a token glides through four stages, the request card fills in field by field and an append-only record writes a line at each stage.
entries.description:
"The life of a request." Choose a kind of request and send it: a token
glides through four stages, the request card fills in field by field and an
append-only record writes a line at each stage. It is an illustration of a
way of working, not a recording of any real system.

stages: [{ id, title, body, glyph, field: { k, v } }]
kinds:  [{ id, label, lines: [one line per stage] }]

entries.name: OrbitNav
entries.summary: An orbit-shaped site navigator. Four routes circle a brand core; the whole object leans toward the pointer; hovering or focusing a node freezes the orbit and the core reads out where it leads. Touch simply taps through.
entries.description:
An orbit-shaped site navigator. Four routes circle a brand core; the whole
object leans toward the pointer; hovering or focusing a node freezes the orbit
and the core reads out where it leads. Touch simply taps through.
Motion is transforms only (compositor), and stands still under reduced motion.

entries.name: OrderPath
entries.summary: An order as a state machine. Pick a scenario and run it: a token walks the path through the states (it can double back, or stop at a terminal state), each state explains itself, and a small ledger says whether anything settled.
entries.description:
An order as a state machine. Pick a scenario and run it: a token walks the
path through the states (it can double back, or stop at a terminal state),
each state explains itself, and a small ledger says whether anything settled.
A teaching diagram of a workflow design — not a trace of a real order.

nodes:     [{ id, title, note, x, y, terminal? }]   (x, y in 0..100)
edges:     [[idA, idB]]
scenarios: [{ id, label, summary, path: [ids], ledger }]

entries.name: PageOutline
entries.summary: A screen reader's-eye view of the page you are reading: its title and language, its headings as an outline, its landmarks, how many places the Tab key stops, and a few things that go wrong. Click a heading to go there.

entries.name: PermissionMatrix
entries.summary: Roles against actions. Toggle what a role may do, switch between "roles only" and "roles plus scope" (own records, own team), then act as a person and see the decision — and the rule that made it.
entries.description:
Roles against actions. Toggle what a role may do, switch between "roles
only" and "roles plus scope" (own records, own team), then act as a person
and see the decision — and the rule that made it.

roles:   [{ id, label, grants: [actionId], scoped: [actionId] }]
actions: [{ id, label, owned: bool }]    owned = needs a record of your own under the scoped model

entries.name: PressKit
entries.summary: Everything someone writing about the company needs to get it right: the company in three lengths (each one copies in a press), a fact sheet where every line copies, and the mark in the files the site itself uses.
entries.description:
Everything someone writing about the company needs to get it right: the
company in three lengths (each one copies in a press), a fact sheet where
every line copies, and the mark in the files the site itself uses.

boilerplates: [{ id, label, text }]   facts: [{ k, v }]   assets: [{ id, name, file, note, preview }]

entries.name: PrincipleStack
entries.summary: Principles as a deck of cards that stack as you scroll: each card sticks just below the last, so the next one slides over it like a card laid on a pile (pure CSS `position: sticky`).
entries.description:
Principles as a deck of cards that stack as you scroll: each card sticks just
below the last, so the next one slides over it like a card laid on a pile
(pure CSS `position: sticky`). Where the browser supports scroll-driven
animation, the buried cards also settle back and dim a touch.

principles: [{ code, title, body, practice, glyph }]

entries.name: ProjectRhythm
entries.summary: How a piece of work moves, as a stepper you can walk (or let walk itself). Each phase says what it produces, what gets decided in it, who is in the room, and the one question that has to be answered before moving on.
entries.description:
How a piece of work moves, as a stepper you can walk (or let walk itself).
Each phase says what it produces, what gets decided in it, who is in the
room, and the one question that has to be answered before moving on.

phases: [{ id, name, purpose, produces[], decides[], who: 'you'|'both'|'north', gate }]

entries.name: ReadinessCheck
entries.summary: Twenty questions to ask before something goes live, in five groups. Answer Yes, Partly, No or Not applicable; the gaps come back as a list to act on, which can be copied or downloaded. Nothing is kept once you leave.

entries.name: ReleaseNotes
entries.summary: The site's history, told in chapters, newest first. The site is not versioned and nothing on it is derived from repository dates, so the chapters carry no dates: they are in the order things happened. Filter by what kind of change.

entries.name: ResearchBench
entries.summary: A small bench of three working studies from this very site. They are live: the numbers in the first are read from this page on this device, the second answers your system's motion setting, the third is a real keyboard row.
entries.description:
A small bench of three working studies from this very site. They are live:
the numbers in the first are read from this page on this device, the second
answers your system's motion setting, the third is a real keyboard row.

experiments: [{ id, label, title, body }]

entries.name: ResourceDesk
entries.summary: The four shelves of the resource centre, each with a live count read from the data behind it and a small peek at what is on it.

entries.name: RuleChain
entries.summary: A rule you can assemble and run. Choose a trigger, a condition and an action, decide whether the condition holds, then run it: a pulse travels WHEN → IF → THEN → LOG and the record appends a line for every run — including the runs where…
entries.description:
A rule you can assemble and run. Choose a trigger, a condition and an action,
decide whether the condition holds, then run it: a pulse travels WHEN → IF →
THEN → LOG and the record appends a line for every run — including the runs
where the rule stops cleanly. Nothing real is triggered; it is a model.

triggers/conditions/actions: [{ id, label }]

entries.name: RunbookWalk
entries.summary: The same incident, two runbooks. One explains the system; the other starts from the symptom.
entries.description:
The same incident, two runbooks. One explains the system; the other starts
from the symptom. Walk either: every block you read adds the time it takes to
read (counted from its actual words), until you reach the first step that
does something.

versions: [{ id, label, blocks: [{ id, kind: 'context'|'action'|'decision', text }] }]

entries.name: SceneLab
entries.summary: A viewer for the site's own Canvas scenes. Choose a study from the list (or with ↑ ↓), change its density, and flip "Still frame" to see the single frame a visitor with reduced motion gets.
entries.description:
A viewer for the site's own Canvas scenes. Choose a study from the list (or
with ↑ ↓), change its density, and flip "Still frame" to see the single frame
a visitor with reduced motion gets. The viewer keeps its place while the scene
underneath it changes.

experiments: [{ id, name, purpose }]

entries.name: ServiceMap
entries.summary: Every service your browser may be asked to contact for this site, one at a time: what it receives, when, whether you can avoid it, and what you would see if you did.
entries.description:
Every service your browser may be asked to contact for this site, one at a
time: what it receives, when, whether you can avoid it, and what you would
see if you did. For the font service the "what you would see" is shown, side
by side, in the real typeface and in the fallback the page would use.

services: [{ id, name, hosts, role, when, receives[], avoid, ifBlocked, fonts? }]

entries.name: SiteDirectory
entries.summary: A directory of every page on the site, built from the same page data that renders them. Type to filter (title, path and the page's opening line), or press "Take me somewhere" to land on a page at random.
entries.description:
A directory of every page on the site, built from the same page data that
renders them. Type to filter (title, path and the page's opening line), or
press "Take me somewhere" to land on a page at random. Rows re-flow with an
eased layout animation as the filter narrows.

entries.name: SplitFlap
entries.summary: A departure board for the careers hero. Two fixed rows state the facts — nothing is listed, introductions are welcome — and a third row flips through the areas of work. Click the third row to flip to the next area yourself.
entries.description:
A departure board for the careers hero. Two fixed rows state the facts —
nothing is listed, introductions are welcome — and a third row flips through
the areas of work. Click the third row to flip to the next area yourself.
The board only cycles while on screen and not at all under reduced motion
(it then rests on the first area).

rows:  [{ label, value }]
cycle: { label, values: [string] }

entries.name: StackMap
entries.summary: The site's stack as slabs, top to bottom: what the visitor touches down to what builds it. Versions and licences are read from the same data as the licences page, so they cannot disagree with it.
entries.description:
The site's stack as slabs, top to bottom: what the visitor touches down to what
builds it. Versions and licences are read from the same data as the licences
page, so they cannot disagree with it.

layers: [{ id, name, blurb, packages: [{ name, why }] }]       (a package with no entry is a thing we wrote)

entries.name: StorageInspector
entries.summary: A live look at what this site has stored in YOUR browser, read straight from cookies, local storage and session storage — not a description of them. Items with the site's own prefix are explained;
entries.description:
A live look at what this site has stored in YOUR browser, read straight from
cookies, local storage and session storage — not a description of them. Items
with the site's own prefix are explained; anything else is flagged as not
coming from this site's code. "Clear" removes only the site's own items.

known: [{ key, purpose }]

entries.name: SystemIndex
entries.summary: A typographic index of the system areas: large rows, a red rule that follows the pointer from row to row, and a floating preview card that trails the cursor (fine pointers only — on touch every row simply shows its own detail).
entries.description:
A typographic index of the system areas: large rows, a red rule that follows
the pointer from row to row, and a floating preview card that trails the
cursor (fine pointers only — on touch every row simply shows its own detail).

items: [{ id, code, title, summary, tags, glyph, to }]

entries.name: TokenInspector
entries.summary: The design tokens, read from the stylesheet this page is wearing. Search them, group them, see what each one is, copy it as var(--name). Nothing here is typed in by hand: change a token in the CSS and this page changes with it.

entries.name: ToolBench
entries.summary: The five browser tools, each with what it does and what it never does. Every one runs in the page: no account, no upload, nothing kept.

entries.name: ToolchainMap
entries.summary: The site's own toolchain as a row of switches. Every stage guards against a kind of problem; switch one off and the ring drops and the problem it would have caught is listed as "could slip through".
entries.description:
The site's own toolchain as a row of switches. Every stage guards against a
kind of problem; switch one off and the ring drops and the problem it would
have caught is listed as "could slip through". A way of seeing why each
check is there — the commands shown are the real ones used on this site.

stages: [{ id, title, command, glyph, checks, slips }]

entries.name: TriggerCompare
entries.summary: Three triggers, one burst of work. Slide the size of the burst, the number of workers and the cron interval, and compare how long the average job waits and how big the backlog gets.

entries.name: TypeScaleTool
entries.summary: A type scale: one base size multiplied again and again by one ratio, so the sizes belong together. Set the base and the ratio, see each step set in type, and copy the sizes as CSS custom properties.

entries.name: WorkPortals
entries.summary: Selected work, composed as portals. Two primary projects sit side by side as big panels; hover or focus one and it widens while the other gives way (flex-grow eases, nothing jumps), its art moves (plates fan out;
entries.description:
Selected work, composed as portals. Two primary projects sit side by side as
big panels; hover or focus one and it widens while the other gives way
(flex-grow eases, nothing jumps), its art moves (plates fan out; the
miniature scene speeds up). Two quieter supporting studies sit below as
slim rows. Stacks vertically on small screens.

entries.name: AltTextLab
entries.summary: Write the alt text for four pictures, each a different problem: a chart, an ornament, an icon in a button, an illustration. Press Check for a short review against common rules, then see one way each could be written.

entries.name: AskDeck
entries.summary: Questions a candidate is welcome to ask, on cards. Turn one to see why it is a good question to ask — and what a good answer would sound like.

entries.name: AskTheSite
entries.summary: Ask the whole site a question. It searches every page's title and text with the same engine as ⌘K and lays the best answers out here, with the sentence that matched. If the answer is not on the site, it says so.

entries.name: AutomationMath
entries.summary: Is it worth automating? Put in how long a job takes, how often it happens, what it costs to build and what it costs to keep running; the page says when it pays for itself, if it ever does. Your numbers; the arithmetic only.

entries.name: BlockPicker
entries.summary: “Which block?” Say what you are trying to show and the page names the block that suits it, with the data that makes it, why it fits, and what people usually reach for instead.
entries.description:
“Which block?” Say what you are trying to show and the page names the block
that suits it, with the data that makes it, why it fits, and what people
usually reach for instead.

intents: [{ id, label, sees, use, why, notThis, sample (a string of the block's data), to? }]

entries.name: Bottleneck
entries.summary: An operation moves at the pace of its slowest step. Five steps, each with people and minutes per item: the slowest is marked, and adding a person anywhere else changes nothing. An invented operation, to show the shape.

entries.name: BundleBuilder
entries.summary: Choose several of the downloadable documents and have them joined into one Markdown file with a contents list — built here, in the page, when you press the button. A pack for a new project, a new teammate, or a handover.

entries.name: CaseExam
entries.summary: Six questions to put to any case study, put to this site's own. For each of the four, the page says plainly what is answered, what is only partly answered and what is not said at all. A way of showing the limits instead of hiding them.

entries.name: ChannelCount
entries.summary: Why coordination gets harder faster than the team grows. Everyone telling everyone needs a channel for every pair of people: the count grows with the square of the headcount. One shared picture needs one per person. The arithmetic, drawn.
entries.description:
Why coordination gets harder faster than the team grows. Everyone telling
everyone needs a channel for every pair of people: the count grows with the
square of the headcount. One shared picture needs one per person. The arithmetic,
drawn. It is a model, not a measurement of any team.

entries.name: ChaosWheel
entries.summary: Break it on purpose. Spin for a way things go wrong, read what should happen and how to rehearse it, and mark the ones you have tried. A wheel because the failure you rehearse is usually the one you thought of; this picks another.

entries.name: CheatSheet
entries.summary: One printable page that holds what the five tools turn on: the thresholds, the ratios, the field ranges, the groups, the headings. Print it, or copy it as plain text.

entries.name: CheckSheet
entries.summary: A checklist to take away: tick things off and a ring fills; copy the whole thing as Markdown (ticks included) or print it. Used by several pages with their own list — each ending is registered under its own name.

entries.name: ClampMaker
entries.summary: Fluid type without media queries: a font size that grows smoothly between two viewport widths and stops at both ends. Set the four numbers; the one line of CSS comes out, and a slider stands in for the browser window.

entries.name: CloserFrame
entries.summary: The common skeleton of a page ending. Each ending is its own composition (see closers/registry.js);
entries.description:
The common skeleton of a page ending. Each ending is its own composition
(see closers/registry.js); this frame only supplies what they share: a mono
"end of page" tag with a drawn rule, an optional headline and lede, and an
optional row of onward links. It is not a call to action — endings summarise
or play out the page they close.

tag     small label, e.g. "End of principles"
title   serif headline (optional — some endings let the object speak)
lede    one sentence under it
onward  [{ label, to }]  where to go next

entries.name: DataShape
entries.summary: “Show this data.” Pick the shape your data has and the page shows the component that suits it, drawn with sample data, with the reason — and the common wrong choice and why it fails.

entries.name: DeprecationNotice
entries.summary: Write the notice before you break anything. Say what is going, what replaces it and how long people have; out come the announcement and the two response headers (Deprecation and Sunset) that let tools notice on their own.

entries.name: DoneBuilder
entries.summary: Write a definition of done. Choose what must be true before work counts as finished; the list becomes a card you can print or paste. It nudges you toward a short list, because a long one is a list nobody checks.

entries.name: DstTrap
entries.summary: Daylight-saving time, as it bites a schedule. Choose a zone and a time of day; the page finds the day or days this year when the clocks change in that zone and says what happens to your time on each: skipped, repeated, or fine.

entries.name: EasePick
entries.summary: The same menu opening, four times, each on a different easing. Pick the one that feels right, then see what the rule of thumb says — and why.

entries.name: EndCredits
entries.summary: Roll credits for the company: not people, but the disciplines, the work and the parts it is made from. It scrolls only while it is on screen, slows to a stop under the pointer, and is a plain list under reduced motion.

entries.name: ExposureDesk
entries.summary: Design what a customer portal shows. Each field of an order says what the usual rule is; switch fields on and off and the preview changes, with a warning for anything that should never leave the building. An invented order.

entries.name: FairLine
entries.summary: Eight things a visitor might do. Call each one fine or not fine; the answer is revealed with the policy's reasoning, and a running tally shows how your reading compares.

entries.name: FinePrint
entries.summary: The disclaimers in genuinely tiny type, with a lens that follows the pointer and reads the line under it at a size you can read.
entries.description:
The disclaimers in genuinely tiny type, with a lens that follows the pointer
and reads the line under it at a size you can read. The lens is decoration:
the real text is always present at its real size, and a switch turns the
whole block up to a comfortable size for anyone without a pointer.

entries.name: FitRadar
entries.summary: Set how much each area of the work draws you, and a radar fills in. The area you lean towards most is named. Nothing is stored or sent — it is a mirror, not a form.

entries.name: FixedStep
entries.summary: Why a game engine does not simply use the time since the last frame. The same ball is dropped three ways: with a tiny step (the answer), with a fixed step that catches up however slowly frames arrive, and with whatever time the frame took.
entries.description:
Why a game engine does not simply use the time since the last frame. The same
ball is dropped three ways: with a tiny step (the answer), with a fixed step that
catches up however slowly frames arrive, and with whatever time the frame took.
An illustration of the idea, not the engine's own code.

entries.name: FlashDeck
entries.summary: Flashcards from the glossary. Read the term, say what it means, turn the card, and mark whether you had it. At the end, the ones still to learn are listed with a way to read more. Nothing is saved.

entries.name: FocusTrap
entries.summary: “Try to escape the dialog.” Open it and press Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape: a log beside it writes down where focus goes — in, round and round inside, and back to the button that opened it. The dialog is the kit’s own.

entries.name: FormBuilder
entries.summary: Choose the fields a form needs and the page builds it from the kit's own components, checks it when you send it (focus goes to the first problem, and a summary is announced), and writes the JSX out so you can take it with you.

entries.name: FrameTape
entries.summary: A strip-chart recorder for this page. Every frame the browser draws is one column on the tape — tall and red when it took long — and three counters tick from the same measurements. Purely live: nothing is kept or sent.

entries.name: FunnelMath
entries.summary: Every step between a first look and a confirmed purchase takes some people away. Set how many carry on at each step (your numbers, invented here) and watch the product of them; then take a step away and see what it is worth.

entries.name: GateRun
entries.summary: A request walks the gates one at a time and stops at the first that says no. Pick a scenario, send it, and watch where it is turned back — and which question it failed. The gates are the page's own four review areas.

entries.name: HistoryBar
entries.summary: The whole history of the site as one chart: a row for each chapter, a bar as long as the number of notes in it, cut into what was added, changed and fixed. The shapes differ as well as the shades, so it reads without colour.

entries.name: Horizon
entries.summary: The company's phases as strata under a horizon: the oldest lies deepest, the newest sits just beneath the surface, and above the line is the part that has not been told yet. Hover or focus a layer to read it.

entries.name: HostScan
entries.summary: "Where has this tab been?" — read from the browser's own list of requests, grouped by host, each one matched against the hosts this site says it uses.

entries.name: HypothesisCard
entries.summary: A small card for a small experiment. A good hypothesis can be wrong, says what would show it, and says when to stop. Fill the five lines; the page flags the usual weaknesses, and the card can be taken away.

entries.name: IntegrationSheet
entries.summary: The agreement that decides whether an integration survives its first bad day. Choose what is sent, when, what happens when it fails and who owns it; out comes a one-page contract to put in front of both teams.

entries.name: KitPicker
entries.summary: “Which component?” — answer what you are trying to do, then narrow it, and the page names the one or two components that fit, with the reason, and links to each in its gallery.

entries.name: LastItem
entries.summary: The classic race: two people press Buy on the last item at once. Step through three ways of handling it and see which ones sell the item twice.

entries.name: LaunchTimeline
entries.summary: The two weeks around a launch, as a track you walk along: what to do at each stop, with the items you can tick and a ring that fills. Arrow keys move between stops. Nothing is saved.

entries.name: LayerSort
entries.summary: Where does it belong? Eight small responsibilities, four layers. Put each in the layer you would give it, then check against the reasoning. There is rarely one possible answer; the point is to say why.

entries.name: LeastPrivilege
entries.summary: Slide how much an account may do and watch the blast radius — what a stolen password or a slip of the mouse could reach — grow with it. The job needs the first three. Everything past that is risk that buys nothing.

entries.name: LifetimeRuler
entries.summary: A ruler of moments. Slide the marker (or use the arrow keys) and each item shows whether it is still alive at that moment — so "how long is it kept?" is answered by watching things go out.

entries.name: Lineage
entries.summary: “Where did this number come from?” Press the figure and follow it down, hop by hop, to the system that produced it, seeing what must be recorded at each hop for the trail to be walkable. An invented figure, to show the idea.

entries.name: LinkBuilder
entries.summary: Pick a page (and, for the long documents, a section) and a format; the link comes out written the way the linking policy asks: the page's own title as the text, the canonical address as the target.

entries.name: LogLine
entries.summary: Write one audit entry. Fill in who, what, to what and why; the server's part (time, request, source) is added for you, and the entry comes out as a structured line you can copy. Nothing is stored.

entries.name: LookupRace
entries.summary: Finding one row among millions. Three ways, with the number of steps each takes as the table grows, and then the real thing: the page builds half a million rows in your browser and times each method for you.

entries.name: MarkDesk
entries.summary: A desk that answers "may I…?". Pick a use from the list (arrow keys move between them); a verdict is stamped onto the slip with the one line that explains it and, where there is one, the page to read next.

entries.name: MarkMisuse
entries.summary: The mark, used wrongly six ways and rightly once — each tile carrying the one-line reason. The wrong versions are real transforms of the real file.

entries.name: MotionModes
entries.summary: One menu opening under three motion policies. The site follows the device's reduced-motion setting, and also offers a calm display setting of its own.

entries.name: NameStyle
entries.summary: How to write the name: four quick choices, each answered the moment you make it, and a one-line style summary at the end.

entries.name: NoticeFile
entries.summary: The notices page's ending: the whole list as a plain NOTICE file you can read here, copy, or download. Built on the spot from the same data as the table.

entries.name: OperationBrief
entries.summary: Write the brief the first conversation needs, before the conversation. Six short answers become a one-page brief you can keep, share or bring. Nothing is sent anywhere: it stays in the page until you copy or download it.

entries.name: PageVitals
entries.summary: The page you are on, weighed: its elements, its requests, its size, its first paint and the frame rate it is managing right now. Every number comes from the browser's own Performance API; nothing is sent anywhere.

entries.name: PagerCard
entries.summary: A one-page runbook template, laid out as a card. Read it here, copy it, or download it as Markdown and fill it in for a real service.

entries.name: PairMatrix
entries.summary: Check a whole palette at once. Paste colours, and every text-on-background pairing is graded in a grid, so the ones that never work are visible before anyone designs with them.

entries.name: ParcelTrack
entries.summary: A tracking line for a report: four stations, a parcel that travels to the one you choose, and who handles that stage. No timings are promised or implied — only the order things happen in.

entries.name: PipelineMaker
entries.summary: Assemble a checks pipeline: choose the checks, put them in order, and a workflow file comes out, with the same sequence as a local script. The commands are placeholders for your project's own.

entries.name: PreMortem
entries.summary: The pre-mortem: imagine a year has passed and the decision turned out badly. What went wrong? Write the reasons, how likely each is, and what you would do about it now. The riskiest come out first, as a table.

entries.name: PrefsPanel
entries.summary: Display preferences for this view — text size, line spacing, contrast, a calm mode and the single-key shortcuts — that take effect at once and last only until the page is reloaded.

entries.name: PrepSheet
entries.summary: The "before a first conversation" sheet: what is worth having to hand. A take-away list, ticked as you go and copied as Markdown.

entries.name: Purge
entries.summary: A purge button for the site's own items in your browser. One press runs a short "wipe", removes only the keys that belong to this site, and shows what is left (which should be nothing of ours).

entries.name: RandomRead
entries.summary: Can't choose? A reel of the guide titles spins and lands on one. It is a dice with manners: it never lands on the same one twice in a row.

entries.name: ReadingColumn
entries.summary: Set a reading column. Slide the measure (characters per line), the line height and the size, and change the face;
entries.description:
Set a reading column. Slide the measure (characters per line), the line height
and the size, and change the face; the text reflows under your hands and the page
says whether each setting is short, comfortable or long — the rules of thumb
behind the site’s Prose component.

entries.name: ReadingList
entries.summary: Build a reading list from the pages of this site: tick what to read, or start from a preset; the list comes out as Markdown with the links and an honest estimate of the time, ready to send to someone.

entries.name: ReadmeMaker
entries.summary: A README that the next person can use. Choose the sections; the skeleton is assembled beside you, with a prompt under every heading saying what belongs there.

entries.name: Receipt
entries.summary: An itemised receipt of what the site holds for this visitor, read live from the browser and "printed" line by line. Copy it as text or print it again.

entries.name: ReviewDraw
entries.summary: A deck of the principles. Draw one and it turns up with a single question to put to your next design review — the principle as something to ask, not something to admire.

entries.name: RoleLens
entries.summary: One record, four people. Each role needs a few of the fields and not the rest. Choose a role and the record rearranges itself: what they need is sharp, what they do not is tucked away but never gone. An invented record, for illustration.

entries.name: ScopeTarget
entries.summary: A target for a vulnerability-reporting scope: the bullseye is what is in scope, the rings outside it are what is not. Hover or focus a ring (or pick it from the list) to read what sits in it.

entries.name: SelfAudit
entries.summary: Four checks you run yourself, on this page, in your browser. Each says what it will look at, then what it found — so "trust us" becomes "look".

entries.name: SigilMaker
entries.summary: A figure drawn from a word. The same word always draws the same shape, so it is a signature rather than a random picture. Download it as an SVG.

entries.name: SizeUp
entries.summary: How big is it, really? Five questions about a system, each a judgement, and the page says what shape of work that adds up to: a focused tool, a platform or a programme, with what changes at each size.

entries.name: SpotTheBug
entries.summary: A review exercise. Read a short piece of code the way a reviewer would, mark the lines you would stop, and press Check. Each real problem comes back with why it matters; lines flagged without cause are named too.

entries.name: StateSheet
entries.summary: The seven states every control owns, shown side by side for three controls, and a live row of the real thing underneath. Tab to it, press it, hover it: the states above are what you are feeling.

entries.name: StatusLedger
entries.summary: An honest ledger of where each document stands. The ticks arrive one by one as the ledger scrolls in; the column nobody has ticked yet says so.

entries.name: SunsetPlan
entries.summary: Plan the end while you are building the start. Choose what applies to the system you are retiring and how much notice people get; out comes an ordered plan counted back from the day it is switched off.

entries.name: SymptomRouter
entries.summary: Start from what is going wrong, not from what the team is called. Choose the symptom closest to yours and the page names the discipline that deals with it, why, and where else to look.

entries.name: TakeawayDeck
entries.summary: The few things worth keeping, as a deck you page through. The top card lifts away to the back; arrow keys work on the deck.

entries.name: TermsCard
entries.summary: The terms on a single card that turns over: what you can do on one side, what not to lean on on the other. Tilts toward the pointer; the flip is a button, so it works without one.

entries.name: ToastBench
entries.summary: Fire the feedback components and watch what each one would announce.

entries.name: TokenPlayground
entries.summary: Change four tokens and watch a small interface follow. The values are set on the preview alone, as custom properties — which is exactly how a real design system restyles everything at once.

entries.name: TrySite
entries.summary: Five things worth trying on this site, each a real control: they open the actual search, the actual shortcuts panel, the actual blueprint mode, the actual calm setting, and a page chosen at random. A way to end by using it.

entries.name: WhatIfRemove
entries.summary: Pull one part out of the stack and see what goes with it. A way of asking how much each dependency really carries. The judgements are ours; the file counts were taken when the page was written.

entries.name: WhichOne
entries.summary: Three questions, one recommendation. Answer them about the job in front of you and the helper names the trigger that fits — and why the other two don't.

entries.name: WizardRun
entries.summary: A four-step flow, walked. The Stepper shows where you are; Next is held back until the step is complete and says why;
entries.description:
A four-step flow, walked. The Stepper shows where you are; Next is held back
until the step is complete and says why; when the step changes, focus moves to
its heading so a keyboard or screen-reader user starts reading at the top of the
new step — and a log beside it writes down what a screen reader would announce.

steps: [{ title, hint, intro }]   (four, in order: details, review, confirm, done)

entries.name: WorkCompare
entries.summary: Put any two of the four side by side. The rows are the things the work pages say; where a row is the same for both it is marked, because what two pieces of work share is as telling as how they differ.

entries.name: PageHero
entries.summary: The scene-backed full-screen hero: a pointer-reactive headline, an intro, actions and — when `hero.aside` names a signature — an interactive object in the right half.
entries.description:
Hero: scene-backed full-screen stage with the pointer-reactive headline and,
when the page declares `hero.aside`, a signature object in the right half
(an orbit navigator, a plate stack, a miniature editor…). The aside is
code-split and reserves its space so it never shifts the layout.

props.name: hero
props.type: { scene, intensity, eyebrow, title, intro, code, status, actions[], aside }

rules: Full-viewport stage (`min-height: 100svh`), content vertically centred. The aside takes the right half on desktop and stacks under 900px.

notes: `hero.actions` are `[{ label, to|href, variant }]`. `hero.aside` is `{ kind, …props }` where `kind` is a signature registered as an aside (see Signatures).

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <PageHero accent="#ff3333" hero={{ scene: 'polar-radar', eyebrow: 'Systems', title: 'Operational platforms.', intro: 'What we build.' }} />

entries.name: HeroTitle
entries.summary: The hero headline: each word rises out of a clipped line (staggered), then the words react to the pointer.
entries.description:
The hero headline. Two motions in sequence, on the same words:
1. entrance — each word rises out of a clipped line, staggered (GSAP);
2. afterwards the words answer the pointer (lift, swell, warm toward red).
Once a word has landed its clip is released so the lift can overshoot the
line. Touch and reduced motion get the entrance only / plain text.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Everything else is passed to the root element.

rules: Uses `--fs-hero`; wraps with the column. Do not set a font size.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <HeroTitle text="Interfaces before noise." />

entries.name: NotFound
entries.summary: "Signal lost": the 404 echoes the address that was asked for and lists the real pages nearest to it, ranked by spelling from the navigation directory.

rules: Full-viewport page section.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <Route path="*" element={<NotFound />} />

entries.name: PageBlock
entries.summary: The block dispatcher: draws one block from `{ type, … }`. Built-in types render directly; the data-first kinds are lazy chunks.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <PageBlock accent="#ff3333" block={{ type: 'callout', tone: 'note', heading: 'Note', body: ['Text.'] }} />

entries.name: PageTemplate
entries.summary: Renders a whole page from a data object: a scene-backed hero, then each block in order, plus a scroll rail for blocks that declare `anchor` + `railLabel`. Sets the document title and wraps the page in a transition.
entries.description:
Renders a full page from a data object: a scene-backed hero followed by an
ordered list of blocks. Blocks that declare `anchor` + `railLabel` also feed
the page's scroll rail. Distinct scene + accent + content + block ordering per
page give every route its own identity while the data stays plain.

rules: A column of full-width sections; every block is `section.section > .container`.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <PageTemplate data={{ key: 'home', title: 'Home', hero: { title: 'Hello.' }, blocks: [] }} />

entries.name: TemplatePage
entries.summary: A route element for a data-driven page: loads the page by key through the registered `loadPage` source (its own code-split chunk), suspends on the route fallback, and shows the 404 when there is no data.

examples.title: Basic
examples.code: <Route path="/systems" element={<TemplatePage routeKey="systems" />} />

entries.name: CalloutBlock
entries.summary: One remark set apart from the text: a note, a tip, a warning.

props.name: block
props.description: The block's data: tone, heading, body[], list[]. Plus the shared keys `anchor`, `railLabel`, `scene`, `intensity`, `eyebrow`, `title`, `intro`.

bestPractices.text: Use it as a block in a page's `blocks[]` (`type: 'callout'`), not on its own.
Nest one block inside another.

rules: Page-width section: `section.section > .container`. Never set a width or padding; the block brings its own.

examples.title: A real callout block
examples.code:
{
  "type": "callout",
  "anchor": "callout",
  "railLabel": "Callout",
  "scene": "topographic-lines",
  "eyebrow": "Block · callout",
  "title": "A callout is for one thing.",
  "tone": "note",
  "heading": "Use it sparingly",
  "body": [
    "Use a callout for the single remark a reader must not miss: an honest limit, an open question, a warning. If every paragraph is a callout, none of them is read.",
    "The kind of remark is written out as a word as well as shown by colour and icon, so it never depends on colour alone."
  ]
}

you leave, and nothing is stored or sent. The count is announced politely as it changes.

{ type: 'checklist', items: [{ label, hint? }], done?: string (said when all are ticked),
 eyebrow?, title?, intro? }

entries.name: CompareBlock
entries.summary: Two or three ways of looking at a choice, side by side.
entries.description:
Two or three ways of looking at a choice, side by side: what to do and what not
to, before and after, this and that. Each column says in words what it is
(`label`), so the sides never depend on colour alone.

{ type: 'compare', columns: [{ label, title, tone?: 'yes'|'no', items: [string] }], verdict?,
 eyebrow?, title?, intro? }

props.name: block
props.description: The block's data: columns[{ label, title, tone, items[] }], verdict. Plus the shared keys `anchor`, `railLabel`, `scene`, `intensity`, `eyebrow`, `title`, `intro`.

bestPractices.text: Use it as a block in a page's `blocks[]` (`type: 'compare'`), not on its own.
Nest one block inside another.

examples.title: A real compare block
examples.code:
{
  "type": "compare",
  "anchor": "compare",
  "railLabel": "Compare",
  "scene": "architectural-grid",
  "eyebrow": "Block · compare",
  "title": "A generic block, or a signature?",
  "columns": [
    {
      "label": "Generic block",
      "title": "Start here",
      "tone": "yes",
      "items": [
        "The content is text, records or links",
        "A standard layout does the job",
        "The kit already has the component",
        "Someone else could use the same block tomorrow"
      ]
    },
    {
      "label": "Signature",
      "title": "When the page is the interaction",
      "items": [
        "The point of the page is something you do",
        "The data has a shape no other page shares",
        "The layout is part of the idea",
        "It would not make sense anywhere else"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "verdict": "Start with a generic block. Reach for a signature when the page’s point is something a reader does and not something a reader reads."
}

there is a series, a line beside it. `note` is required in spirit: say where the
figures come from, or that they are sample data. This site shows no number it
cannot stand behind.

Designed precision cursor. A tight core dot tracks the pointer exactly while
a reticle follows with a little lag. Hovering elements that declare
data-cursor="link|card|nav|redacted|audio" morph the reticle into a
context-appropriate state. Fine-pointer only; disabled under reduced motion.
No React state on mousemove — everything is refs + GSAP quickTo + classList.

entries.name: BootSequence
entries.summary: The cinematic intro: brand and a START control, a HUD calibration with terminal lines, then the lift. Starts the ambient track inside the click when one is configured.
entries.description:
Cinematic boot / entry experience.
intro  -> brand + START control glide in
booting-> HUD calibration: grid, brackets, terminal feed, counter,
         kinetic block swipes, perspective matrix
done   -> overlay dissolves and the site is revealed (onComplete)

START is a real user gesture, so it also begins the ambient track (through
the shared AudioProvider — the navbar control follows the same status). If
the browser refuses playback the intro carries on silently and the navbar
shows "TAP TO PLAY". Skip never touches audio.

Plays at most once per session (the shell decides whether to mount it). A
Skip control is always available so the user is never trapped. Reduced
motion collapses to a quiet handoff.

onComplete fires the moment the reveal begins (so the shell can animate
the site in underneath), and onExited fires once the overlay has fully
lifted away and is safe to unmount — together they replace the old hard
cut with a crossfade.

Props: onComplete(), onExited()

props.name: onExited
props.description: Called when the overlay has fully faded and can unmount.

rules: Fixed full-viewport (`--z-boot`); the page cannot scroll while it is mounted.

examples.title: Basic

entries.name: ScanlineOverlay
entries.summary: Fixed, full-viewport CRT scanline veil. Extremely subtle, static and pointer-events none.
entries.description:
Fixed, full-viewport CRT scanline veil. Extremely subtle, static and
pointer-events none.

It used to carry a 28vh band that crossed the screen forever. That one
infinite loop cost ~15 fps while scrolling (measured A/B on the home page,
46 -> 57 fps with it removed): a large translucent layer re-composited over
every animating canvas, all the time, for an effect almost nobody could see.
Removed on purpose — motion on this site is for state, not ambience.

entries.name: SynthesisCanvas
entries.summary: SynthesisCanvas — the heavy, procedural half of the cinematic. A single canvas drives every particle/ring/grid layer for all eleven phases.
entries.description:
SynthesisCanvas — the heavy, procedural half of the cinematic. A single
canvas drives every particle/ring/grid layer for all eleven phases. It does
NOT own a loop: the parent's master GSAP timeline calls `render(t)` once per
frame with the sequence time in seconds, so there is exactly one clock for
the whole experience (canvas + DOM stay in perfect sync, trivial cleanup).

Exposes via ref: render(seconds) and a one-shot still(seconds).

entries.name: SystemSynthesisOverlay
entries.summary: SystemSynthesisOverlay — the full-screen takeover. NOT a page, NOT a player.
entries.description:
SystemSynthesisOverlay — the full-screen takeover. NOT a page, NOT a player.
Mounts already playing, owns the whole viewport (nav/cursor hidden + scroll
locked by ExperienceProvider), exposes only a minimal SKIP + a subtle system
HUD, and dissolves back into the live site on completion or skip.

entries.name: Footer
entries.summary: The site footer — a directory of the whole site, not a second navigation bar: six columns of grouped links, live section counts, the status and the legal row. Collapses to disclosures on a phone.
entries.description:
Site footer — a directory of the whole site, not a second navigation bar.
The primary menu carries Work, Systems, Development and Company; this leads to
the rest: how the company works, the guides, the tools, the trust material and
the legal documents. Six columns with named groups, a search field, a row of
the site's sections with live page counts, a strip of what is new, a legal
row, a marquee that scroll velocity pushes, a back-to-top ring that fills as
you read, the visitor's local time, and a wordmark whose letters answer the
pointer. Columns fold into disclosures on a phone.

rules: Page-width section. Six columns on a desktop, disclosures under 900px. Never set a width on it.

notes: Columns come from `footerColumns`, the legal line from `footerLegalRow`, counts from `siteSections` (see `applyNavigation`).
It shows the brand mark from `assetResolver`.

entries.name: RouteAnnouncer
entries.summary: Tells assistive technology that a new page has opened: waits for the title to settle, says it in a polite status region, and moves focus to `main`.
entries.description:
Tells assistive technology that a new page has opened.

Moving between pages here does not reload the document, so a screen reader
hears nothing unless something says so. Each page sets document.title when
it mounts (and the page it replaces resets it on the way out), so this waits
for the title to stop changing and then reads it out in a polite live region.
If the link that was used went with the old page, keyboard focus is handed to
the new page's main region, so the next Tab starts from its content and not
from the top of the site.

rules: Visually hidden; no layout.

entries.description:
Top-level frame. Owns the boot gate, scroll-lock, designed cursor, light
global overlays, navigation, and footer. There is NO global animated
background — every section declares its own scene (SectionScene). Audio
lives in AudioProvider and only starts through the explicit audio control.

Nest it, or use it for an embedded widget — it fixes elements to the viewport and locks scroll during the intro.

notes: The boot intro shows once per browser session; set `sessionStorage["hnx.boot.complete"] = "1"` to skip it (embeds, tests).
The page cannot scroll while the intro is mounted.

entries.name: AdvancedNavbar
entries.summary: The primary navigation: a hover-intent controller and a wide full-screen-width menu (categories on the left, pages across the right). Reads its groups from the navigation config.
entries.description:
Primary navigation with an intentional hover-intent controller and a wide,
full-screen-width menu (categories on the left, pages across the right). The
menu opens only on a deliberate dwell and closes on
every dismissal path: route change, link click, outside pointer, Escape,
scroll, window blur, focus-out, and the mobile menu opening. Single-child
groups never deploy a panel — they are plain links.

Flow details:
- `revealed` (set by the shell as the intro lifts) glides the bar, then its
parts, into place — the navbar is on screen the moment the site is.
- the scrolled background is a layer whose OPACITY eases in (gradients cannot
be transitioned, which is what made it jump), with the hairline drawing
out from the centre.
- one ink indicator springs between links instead of each link toggling its
own underline.

A group with one child is a plain link and never opens a panel.

entries.description:
Command palette / site search.

A fixed overlay rendered in a portal and anchored to the TOP of the viewport
(never vertically re-centred), so growing or shrinking result lists cannot
make it jump. It searches page titles AND body copy / case-study text and
shows the best matching excerpt for each page.

closes · Tab stays inside the dialog. Click outside dismisses. Focus returns
to where it was.

entries.name: BlueprintLayer
entries.summary: Blueprint mode. `html.blueprint` outlines every marked part of the page (see styles/fx.css);
entries.description:
Blueprint mode. `html.blueprint` outlines every marked part of the page (see
styles/fx.css); this layer names them: a small label pinned to the corner of
each element that carries a `data-fx` marker, and a count of how many
distinct marked details this page has. It re-reads the page twice a second
(lazy chunks arrive late) and repositions on scroll, only while the mode is
on, and never touches layout.

entries.summary: Site-wide single-key shortcuts that belong to no one page: `?` opens the shortcuts panel and `B` switches blueprint mode. Switchable off for WCAG 2.1.4 (`html[data-keys="off"]`).
entries.description:
Site-wide single-key shortcuts that belong to no one page:
?  opens the shortcuts panel
B  switches blueprint mode (outlines and names the marked parts of a page)
Search (Ctrl/⌘ K and /) lives with the search itself. Nothing fires while you
are typing, while a modifier is held, or before the intro has finished — and
the single-key ones can be switched off in the display preferences (WCAG 2.1.4).

entries.description:
The "?" panel: a short list of the keys that do something here. It is a real

backdrop close it, the page behind stops scrolling — and it eases in and out
rather than appearing. Rows light their caps as you press the real keys.

entries.name: TransitionOverlay
entries.summary: The route "current": navigating does not cover the screen — a thin red line travels the viewport with the destination written at its end. Skipped under reduced motion.
entries.description:
Route "current". Navigating does not cover the screen. A thin red line (with a
soft wash trailing behind it and the destination written at its end) travels
across the viewport while the old page eases out and the new one eases in, so
there is always something moving and never a blank frame. Pure CSS transform
+ opacity, no blur and no filter, pointer-events: none, one-shot, and skipped
under reduced motion. The motif's direction follows the section being entered.

rules: Fixed, pointer-events none, `--z-route-transition`. No layout.

entries.name: Reveal
entries.summary: Reveal — animate a single element into view with a named profile. <Reveal profile="slideLeft" as="p">…</Reveal> Honours reduced motion (static).
entries.description:
Reveal — animate a single element into view with a named profile.
<Reveal profile="slideLeft" as="p">…</Reveal>
Honours reduced motion (static).

IMPORTANT: this component must NOT re-render on scroll. It used to subscribe
to the fast-scroll governor and swap its `variants`/`viewport` objects on
every scroll burst — which made Framer Motion tear down and recreate the
`whileInView` observer, replaying the entrance over and over (sections
visibly "collapsing and reappearing" while scrolling). The variants and
viewport config are memoised here so their identity is stable; with
`once: true` Motion keeps the original observer, fires the entrance exactly
once, then disconnects.

`will-change` / `filter` / `clip-path` housekeeping lives in the profiles
themselves (see `withHousekeeping` in revealProfiles.js).

entries.description:
Split-text reveal. Each character (or word) rises out of a clipped line
with a staggered cadence — the signature "kinetic" headline motion.
Pure CSS spans, no paid SplitText plugin. Accessible: the visible spans
are aria-hidden and the original string is exposed via aria-label.

Props:
